paper_sections.title: Aging of visual word perception is related to decreased segregation within and beyond the word network in the brain
Data preprocessing for resting-state fMRI data

Between-group difference in resting-state functional connectivity

description.value: The study examined age-related differences in visual word perception using behavioral visual matching, task fMRI, resting-state seed-based functional connectivity, and correlations between connectivity and word-matching performance.

design.value: The study compared healthy older adults with young adults using a word localizer task, resting-state fMRI, and word- and symbol-form matching tasks. Word-selective ventral occipitotemporal regions were identified separately for each age group and used as seeds for within- and beyond-word-network functional connectivity analyses.

task_description.value: This study first collected resting-state fMRI data from all participants in a quiet state.

instructions.value: They were asked to keep their heads as still as possible.

task_description.value: The localizer task involved a simple location judgment task. Visual stimuli were divided into two types: Chinese characters and phase-separated Chinese characters. The task included 16 blocks of visual stimulation and 16 blocks of fixation in a balanced order, with each block lasting 15 s.

instructions.value: Participants judged the location of the stimulus by pressing the corresponding button as accurately and quickly as possible.

stimuli.value: Chinese characters and phase-separated Chinese characters, presented on either the left or right side of the fixation point; each picture was presented for 250 ms followed by a 750-ms inter-stimulus interval.

task_description.value: After completing all MRI scans, participants performed two visual matching tasks—word matching and symbol-form matching—in another room. The test consisted of 60 trials, with randomized stimuli and same/different trials.

design_type.value: same procedure for word matching and symbol-form matching

instructions.value: Participants must quickly determine whether the two words on the screen are identical and press the corresponding button as swiftly and accurately as possible.

stimuli.value: 30 new pictures of words and 30 new pictures of symbols, all in stick figure style. The stimuli were black against the background, and the visual angle of each stimulus was 1.1.

instrument.value: GE 3-Tesla MRI scanner (MR-750, GE Medical Systems, Milwaukee, WI)

description.value: Echo Planar Imaging (EPI) was used to obtain rs-fMRI data. The acquisition used 43 axial slices, a flip angle of 90°, a field of view of 220 × 220 mm², and a matrix size of 64 × 64.

description.value: Echo Planar Imaging (EPI) was used to obtain task-fMRI data. The acquisition used 43 axial slices, a flip angle of 90°, a field of view of 220 × 220 mm², and a matrix size of 64 × 64.
Task-fMRI data were processed using the DPABI toolkit. The preprocessing steps were identical to those in the previous study.

description.value: Resting-state fMRI data were preprocessed using the DPABI toolkit, following the same procedure as the previous study.

model_settings.value: The phase-scattered Chinese characters were used as a baseline, and activation caused by the Chinese character images was compared. The linear contrast image (Chinese characters vs. scattered Chinese characters) was calculated for each participant.
A one-sample t-test was performed to obtain the group-level activation map. The most activated voxels within the left and right vOT regions were selected using FDR correction, q < 0.05.

Pearson correlation coefficients were calculated between the averaged time courses of the two vOT ROIs, and between each ROI time course and every voxel in the brain. Correlation coefficients were transformed to z-values using Fisher’s r-to-z transformation.

estimator.value: Pearson correlation coefficient with Fisher’s r-to-z transformation

model_settings.value: The between-subject variable was age and the within-subject variable was stimulus type.

Two-sample t-tests compared connectivity values between older and young adult groups. Gender was included as a covariate for connectivity beyond the word network. Gaussian Random Field theory was used for multiple comparison correction, with p < 0.001 at the voxel level and p < 0.05 at the cluster level, two-tailed.

A Pearson correlation coefficient was calculated between the mean connectivity value of each cluster showing significant between-group differences and the IES from the word-matching task. These correlation analyses used p < 0.05.
Partial correlations were computed between connectivity values in each cluster and the IES from the word-matching task, controlling for the IES from the symbol-form matching task.
